classification.difficultyReason: Factor the quadratic divisor, evaluate the polynomial and remainder at its roots, and solve two linear equations.

content.prompt: When $P(x)=x^5+ax^2+bx+2$ is divided by $x^2-x-2$, the remainder is $2x+1$. Find $a$ and $b$.

answer.short:
$a=-\dfrac{11}{2},\quad b=-\dfrac{7}{2}$

Substitute $x=2$ and $x=-1$ into the division identity and solve simultaneously.
answer.worked:
By the division transformation,
$$P(x)=(x-2)(x+1)Q(x)+2x+1.$$
Substitute $x=2$ and $x=-1$:
$$\begin{align*}
P(2)&=32+4a+2b+2=5\\
4a+2b&=-29\\
P(-1)&=-1+a-b+2=-1\\
a-b&=-2.
\end{align*}$$
Solve simultaneously:
$$\begin{align*}
b&=a+2\\
4a+2(a+2)&=-29\\
6a&=-33\\
a&=-\frac{11}{2}\\
b&=-\frac{11}{2}+2=-\frac{7}{2}.
\end{align*}$$
